Definition: from G2954; a Cyprian (Cypriot), i.e. inhabitant of Cyprus:--of Cyprus.
BiblicalUsage: Men of Cyprus are the believers who carried the gospel out of Jerusalem. In Acts 4:36 Barnabas is introduced as a Levite of the country of Cyprus, and in Acts 11:20 men of Cyprus and Cyrene came to Antioch and preached the Lord Jesus to the Grecians.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the Cypriots matter because they crossed the line first: the gospel had gone to Jews only, and it was men of Cyprus who spoke it to Greeks at Antioch, and the church there was born.
